description: Senior-engineer rubric for one-shot, professional-grade software. Scores quality, robustness, polish, and deployability — NOT cost or speed. Each dimension is scored 0-5; weighted total is the headline number. Anchors describe what each level looks like in the diff.

dimensions.label: Correctness
dimensions.description: Does it actually do what was asked, with the right semantics? Hidden gates passing is a hard floor.

anchors.0: Does not run, does not address the task, or fails the visible task.
anchors.1: Surface-level only — happy path only, breaks on the first non-trivial input.
anchors.2: Most of the visible task works; obvious edge cases are wrong.
anchors.3: Visible task works end-to-end; some subtle edge cases mishandled.
anchors.4: Visible task plus most of the obvious-but-tricky cases handled correctly.
anchors.5: All visible behaviour correct, including the hidden-gate fixtures a senior reviewer would inject.

dimensions.label: Robustness & defensive design
dimensions.description: Adversarial inputs, untrusted data, error paths, retries, timeouts. The 'thought of every angle' axis.

anchors.0: No input validation. Trusts strings as commands. No error handling.
anchors.1: Token validation — sanity checks but trivially bypassable.
anchors.2: Error paths exist for the obvious failures; injection / escape are wide open.
anchors.3: Untrusted data is escaped or quoted; failures degrade rather than crash.
anchors.4: Multiple defensive layers; clearly-named primitives for the dangerous operations; tests cover the adversarial cases.
anchors.5: Adversarial mindset visible throughout: argument arrays not interpolated strings, allow-lists, path traversal blocks, encoding-aware boundaries, explicit failure modes documented.

dimensions.label: Polish & code quality
dimensions.description: Readable names, clean abstractions, sensible structure, comments where they add value, no dead code.

anchors.0: Hard to follow. Cryptic names, copy-paste, magic numbers.
anchors.1: Works but feels rushed — inconsistent naming, missing types, no comments.
anchors.2: Reasonable structure; some rough edges (overlong functions, ad-hoc helpers).
anchors.3: Clear intent throughout; types where it matters; comments explain non-obvious choices.
anchors.4: A senior would land it with minor nits.
anchors.5: Polish you would expect from a staff engineer's PR — abstractions feel inevitable, comments explain *why*, no extraneous code.

dimensions.label: Tests & verifiability
dimensions.description: Tests that actually pin behaviour, especially the adversarial cases. Type-checks, assertions, repro instructions.

anchors.1: Smoke test only — proves nothing about the dangerous cases.
anchors.2: Some unit tests; happy path coverage.
anchors.3: Tests cover happy path plus a couple of failure cases.
anchors.4: Tests pin the adversarial cases that motivated the task.
anchors.5: Tests are themselves a spec — anyone reading them learns the invariants the code enforces.

dimensions.label: Architectural fit
dimensions.description: Changes flow with the surrounding codebase: existing patterns, types, file layout. No drive-by refactors that overflow scope.

anchors.0: Wholesale departure from existing patterns. Random files moved.
anchors.1: Conflicts with existing conventions (mismatched style, duplicated helpers).
anchors.2: Mostly fits; a few unforced inconsistencies.
anchors.3: Matches existing patterns; uses existing helpers where they exist.
anchors.4: Code reads as if it has always been there.
anchors.5: Improves the surrounding code's coherence without expanding scope.

dimensions.label: Deployability
dimensions.description: Can this ship? Type-check, build, no half-finished migrations or TODO-as-feature, no broken imports.

anchors.1: Builds with warnings; obvious runtime issues on first launch.
anchors.2: Builds; some parts visibly unfinished or stubbed.
anchors.3: Builds and runs the happy path.
anchors.4: Builds, type-checks, all visible features work.
anchors.5: Production-ready: type-checks clean, public gates green, no TODOs masquerading as features, behaves correctly on a fresh checkout.

judging_protocol.blinded: Judges must not know which adapter produced the diff. Variant labels (`spark`, `claude`, `codex`) are stripped from artifacts before judging.
judging_protocol.position_randomized: When comparing two diffs, the harness randomizes A/B order independently per judge.
judging_protocol.independent: Each judge sees only the rubric and the diff. Judges do not see each other's verdicts.
judging_protocol.structured_output: Each judge returns JSON with per-dimension scores (0-5), a per-dimension justification, a per-issue list, and an overall verdict. Parse failures retried once.
judging_protocol.panel_aggregation: Per-dimension: mean of three judges. Total: weighted mean of dimension means. Disagreement: max - min per dimension; flagged when > 2.
